expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: "No. That test could not have failed here." and "it's a check that cannot go red in this failure mode, which is worse than no test because it reads as coverage."

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: "`COALESCE(revenue, 0)` makes 'no data' and 'no revenue' the same value. The pipeline has no way to express *unknown*, so a total join failure renders as a business fact."

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: "Daily reconciliation: warehouse total vs billing source"

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: "Assert *between* load and publish. A test that runs after publication has already lost."

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: "Schema contract at ingest: assert expected columns/types, fail the load on a rename"

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: "Join match-rate assertion before publish (`matched / total`), staged → tested → promoted"

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: "Your detection latency *was* the three weeks" and recommends daily reconciliation to fix it

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: Describes mechanism ("converts a loud failure into a quiet number") but doesn't explain why the quiet number is dangerous, only that it swallows the signal.
